case_studies.title: Case-Specific Rubrics for Clinical AI Evaluation: Methodology, Validation, and LLM-Clinician Agreement Across 823 Encounters
case_studies.abstract: Objective. Clinical AI documentation systems require evaluation methodologies that are clinically valid, economically viable, and sensitive to iterative changes. Methods requiring expert review per scoring instance are too slow and expensive for safe, iterative deployment. We present a case-specific, clinician-authored rubric methodology for clinical AI evaluation and examine whether LLM-generated rubrics can approximate clinician agreement. Materials and Methods. Twenty clinicians authored 1,646 rubrics for 823 clinical cases (736 real-world, 87 synthetic) across primary care, psychiatry, onc
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating clinical AI documentation systems is addressed through the development of case-specific rubrics. The AI approach involves utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate rubrics that approximate clinician agreement. The outcome shows promise in reducing the need for expert review per scoring instance, making clinical AI evaluation more efficient and cost-effective.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this methodology, AI practitioners can utilize LLMs to generate case-specific rubrics for clinical AI evaluation, allowing for more efficient and cost-effective evaluation processes. By leveraging clinician-authored rubrics as a reference point, practitioners can fine-tune their LLM models to achieve higher accuracy and agreement with human clinicians.
case_studies.monetisation: A concrete business opportunity arises from developing and commercializing a clinical AI evaluation platform that integrates LLM-generated rubrics, offering healthcare institutions a more efficient and cost-effective solution for evaluating their clinical AI systems. This platform could be marketed as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution, providing a recurring revenue stream for the company and helping to drive the adoption of clinical AI systems in healthcare.

case_studies.title: Leveraging LLMs for Multi-File DSL Code Generation: An Industrial Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on general-purpose code generation, yet their applicability to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) remains underexplored, especially for repository-scale change generation spanning multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language (NL) instruction. We report an industrial case study at BMW that adapts code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL that drives downstream Java/TypeScript code generation. We develop an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction, multi-file task r
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the challenge of generating and modifying domain-specific language (DSL) code across multiple files using large language models (LLMs). The authors develop an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction and multi-file task generation, adapting code-oriented LLMs for an industrial setting at BMW. The outcome demonstrates the potential of LLMs in enterprise DSL code generation, with implications for increased efficiency and productivity.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing tailored datasets and fine-tuning LLMs for specific DSLs and industrial contexts. By leveraging the capabilities of LLMs, practitioners can automate complex code generation tasks and improve the overall development process.
case_studies.monetisation: The study highlights a concrete business opportunity in developing and marketing LLM-based solutions for enterprise DSL code generation, particularly in industries with complex software development needs. Companies can capitalize on this technology by offering customized LLM-powered tools and services for automated code generation, reducing development time and costs for clients.

case_studies.title: Less Is More: Engineering Challenges of On-Device Small Language Model Integration in a Mobile Application
case_studies.abstract: On-device Small Language Models (SLMs) promise fully offline, private AI experiences for mobile users (no cloud dependency, no data leaving the device). But is this promise achievable in practice? This paper presents a longitudinal practitioner case study documenting the engineering challenges of integrating SLMs (Gemma 4 E2B, 2.6B parameters; Qwen3 0.6B, 600M parameters) into Palabrita, a production Android word-guessing game. Over a 5-day development sprint comprising 204 commits (~90 directly AI-related), the system underwent a radical transformation: from an ambitious design where the LLM
case_studies.summary: The case study explores the engineering challenges of integrating Small Language Models (SLMs) into a mobile application, specifically a word-guessing game called Palabrita. The authors employed a longitudinal practitioner case study approach, documenting the integration of two SLMs, Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3 0.6B, over a 5-day development sprint. The outcome of the study highlights the radical transformation of the system, with 204 commits and a significant portion of them being AI-related, showcasing the potential of on-device SLMs for offline, private AI experiences.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the lessons from this case study, AI practitioners should focus on iterative development and rapid prototyping when integrating SLMs into mobile applications, emphasizing the importance of adaptability and flexibility in the development process. By doing so, they can overcome the engineering challenges associated with on-device SLM integration and create more efficient, private, and user-friendly AI experiences.
case_studies.monetisation: The integration of SLMs into mobile applications, such as Palabrita, presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and market AI-powered games and tools that prioritize user privacy and offline functionality. By capitalizing on the potential of on-device SLMs, businesses can create new revenue streams and differentiate themselves from competitors, particularly in the gaming and education sectors.

case_studies.title: On-Device Vision Training, Deployment, and Inference on a Thumb-Sized Microcontroller
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline, comprising data acquisition, two-layer CNN training with Adam optimization, and real-time inference, executing entirely on a microcontroller-class device costing $15-40 USD. Unlike cloud-based workflows that require external infrastructure and conceal the computational pipeline from the practitioner, this system implements every step of the core ML lifecycle in approximately 1,750 lines of readable C++ that compiles in under one minute using the Arduino IDE, with no external ML dependencies. Running on the S
case_studies.summary: The problem of relying on cloud-based workflows for machine learning is addressed by developing an on-device vision machine learning pipeline. The AI approach involves using a two-layer CNN with Adam optimization, trained and deployed on a microcontroller-class device. The outcome is a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline that can be implemented in approximately 1,750 lines of readable C++ code.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize microcontroller-class devices to develop and deploy machine learning models, allowing for real-time inference and reduced reliance on external infrastructure. By using the Arduino IDE and C++ code, practitioners can compile and deploy their models quickly and efficiently.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of this on-device vision machine learning pipeline presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to create and market low-cost, AI-powered devices for various applications. This technology can be adapted for use in industries such as healthcare, security, and transportation, providing a clear product opportunity and potential for significant revenue generation.

case_studies.title: A Deployable Embodied Vision-Language Navigation System with Hierarchical Cognition and Context-Aware Exploration
case_studies.abstract: Bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment remains a key challenge in intelligent robotic systems, where perception, reasoning, and planning must operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution. In vision-language navigation (VLN), existing approaches often face a fundamental trade-off between strong reasoning capabilities and efficient deployment on real-world platforms. In this paper, we present a deployable embodied VLN system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platform
case_studies.summary: The problem of bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment in intelligent robotic systems is addressed in this paper. The AI approach presented is a deployable embodied vision-language navigation system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platforms. The outcome is a system that can operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution while maintaining strong reasoning capabilities.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration algorithms that can efficiently operate on real-world platforms. By integrating computer vision and natural language processing, practitioners can create more robust and efficient navigation systems for various applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The presented system has a clear product opportunity in areas such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart home devices, where efficient and robust navigation is crucial. Companies can adapt this technology to develop innovative products, such as robotic assistants or autonomous cleaning devices, that can navigate and interact with their environment effectively.

case_studies.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive. By optimizing the next action given the current observation without evaluating potential futures, they are brittle to the compounding failure modes of long-horizon tasks. Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive control to plan-and-act by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency, then com
case_studies.summary: The problem of reliable long-horizon execution in industrial robotic manipulation is addressed by shifting from reactive control to plan-and-act approaches. The AI approach used in Cortex 2.0 generates candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency. The outcome is a more robust and efficient control system capable of handling changing object distributions and embodiments.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing planning-based methods that evaluate potential futures and optimize for long-horizon execution. By integrating visual latent space representations with scoring mechanisms for expected success and efficiency, practitioners can create more reliable and adaptable control systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of Cortex 2.0 presents a concrete business opportunity in the automation and robotics sector, where companies can integrate this technology to improve the efficiency and reliability of their industrial manipulation systems. By licensing or productizing this technology, companies can generate revenue and establish themselves as leaders in the field of industrial robotics and automation.

case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. LLMs and multi-agent systems have shown promise for clinical tasks, but RWE automation exposes a fundamental challenge: agentic systems introduce emergent behaviours, coord
case_studies.summary: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM) has enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data, but generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process. The proposed solution, FastOMOP, utilizes a foundational architecture for reliable agentic real-world evidence generation on OMOP CDM data, leveraging AI and multi-agent systems. This approach has the potential to automate RWE generation, but its development and implementation are still in the conceptual phase.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners should focus on designing and testing agentic systems that can effectively navigate the complexities of OMOP CDM data, ensuring the reliability and safety of the generated RWE. Additionally, they should consider the emergent behaviors that may arise from these systems and develop strategies to mitigate potential risks.
case_studies.monetisation: The FastOMOP concept presents a business opportunity for companies to develop and market automated RWE generation solutions, potentially disrupting the current manual process and creating a new revenue stream. By targeting pharmaceutical companies, research institutions, and healthcare organizations, these solutions could provide significant value by reducing the time and cost associated with RWE generation, while improving the quality and reliability of the evidence.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, Healthcare AI, NLP, MLOps

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The on-robot deployment of Vision-Language-Action models is hindered by the need for real-time inference under strict cost and energy constraints. To address this, the authors propose a systematic analysis of model-hardware co-characterization to evaluate the suitability of various edge accelerators for VLA deployment. The study's outcome highlights the potential of right-sized edge devices to facilitate low-cost VLA deployment, but the practical implementation and real-world impact remain to be seen.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the trade-offs between cost, energy, and time when selecting edge accelerators for their VLA models, and by exploring model-hardware co-characterization to optimize their deployments. By doing so, they can potentially accelerate the development of more efficient and cost-effective on-robot VLA systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The findings from this study could be monetized by developing and marketing specialized edge accelerators tailored to the needs of VLA models, or by offering consulting services to help companies optimize their VLA deployments for on-robot use cases. Companies could also leverage the insights from this research to create more efficient and cost-effective VLA-powered robots for various industries, such as manufacturing, logistics, or healthcare.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, Computer Vision, NLP, MLOps

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The current static benchmarks for evaluating AI agents have limitations, as they only measure performance at a fixed point in time. AgentPulse is a continuous evaluation framework that assesses AI agents across multiple factors, including benchmark performance, adoption signals, community sentiment, and ecosystem health. By using this framework, researchers can gain a more comprehensive understanding of AI agent performance and impact in real-world deployments.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the lessons from AgentPulse, AI practitioners can develop more comprehensive evaluation frameworks that incorporate multiple signals and factors to assess AI agent performance. By doing so, they can identify areas for improvement and optimize their AI agents for better real-world performance and adoption.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a business opportunity for companies to develop and offer continuous evaluation services for AI agents, helping organizations optimize their AI deployments and improve overall performance. This could be achieved through a subscription-based model, where companies pay for access to the evaluation framework and receive regular updates on their AI agent's performance and areas for improvement.

case_studies.title: Personalized Worked Example Generation from Student Code Submissions using Pattern-based Knowledge Components
case_studies.abstract: Adaptive programming practice often relies on fixed libraries of worked examples and practice problems, which require substantial authoring effort and may not correspond well to the logical errors and partial solutions students produce while writing code. As a result, students may receive learning content that does not directly address the concepts they are working to understand, while instructors must either invest additional effort in expanding content libraries or accept a coarse level of personalization. We present an approach for knowledge-component (KC) guided educational content generat
case_studies.summary: The problem of fixed libraries of worked examples and practice problems in adaptive programming practice is addressed through a pattern-based knowledge component approach, generating personalized worked examples from student code submissions. This AI approach utilizes knowledge-component guided educational content generation to provide tailored learning content. The outcome is a more personalized learning experience, directly addressing the concepts students are working to understand.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize pattern-based knowledge components to generate personalized educational content, focusing on the specific errors and concepts students are struggling with. By integrating this approach into existing adaptive learning systems, practitioners can create a more effective and personalized learning environment.
case_studies.monetisation: A concrete business opportunity for this approach is to develop an adaptive learning platform that integrates the personalized worked example generation capability, offering it as a subscription-based service to educational institutions. This platform can also provide instructors with tools to create and customize their own knowledge components, generating additional revenue streams.

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. During offline training, GradMAP embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual le
case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices is addressed through a novel learning approach, leveraging a gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning method called GradMAP. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent, allowing for fully decentralized deployment while respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This approach enables efficient online decision-making without communication among agents, offering a potential solution for optimizing grid-edge flexibility.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on integrating differentiable physical models into their learning frameworks, enabling the incorporation of domain-specific constraints and physics. By doing so, they can develop more effective and efficient solutions for complex, decentralized systems, such as those found in grid-edge device coordination.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP approach presents a clear opportunity for product development in the energy and utilities sector, where optimizing grid-edge flexibility can lead to significant cost savings and improved efficiency. A company could develop a commercial solution based on GradMAP, offering it as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform for utilities and grid operators to manage their distributed energy resources more effectively.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. Centralized algorithms face high control-data overhead and computational load, while distributed approaches often perform far from optimally. The O-RAN architecture introduces two tiers of RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling hierarchical network-management schemes. This work proposes Tandem Apps: a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both controllers. We show how to design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve an agile, low-comp
case_studies.summary: The growing complexity of mobile networks has made management and optimization challenging, with centralized algorithms facing high control-data overhead and computational load. This work proposes Tandem Apps, a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs) in the O-RAN architecture, to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. The proposed approach aims to optimize cell on/off switching, a crucial use case in wireless network management.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can leverage the O-RAN architecture and design Tandem Apps by splitting optimization mechanisms into architectural and functional components. By doing so, they can develop hierarchical network-management schemes that balance computational load and control-data overhead.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed Tandem Apps can be monetized by developing a product that provides optimized network management solutions for mobile network operators, potentially reducing their operational costs and improving network efficiency. This product can be adapted to various network scenarios, offering a significant business opportunity in the telecommunications industry.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. We present Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The framework is organiz
case_studies.summary: The problem of controllable diffusion methods is that they are typically developed as isolated systems, making it difficult to reuse infrastructure or transfer capabilities. The AI approach presented is Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The outcome of this framework is the ability to reuse infrastructure, transfer capabilities, and compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this framework by developing plugins for specific controllable diffusion methods, allowing for greater flexibility and reusability across different tasks and backbones. By using Diffusion Templates, practitioners can simplify their development pipeline and focus on developing new capabilities rather than rebuilding existing infrastructure.
case_studies.monetisation: The Diffusion Templates framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing AI-powered products, as it enables the creation of more flexible and customizable diffusion models. By leveraging this framework, companies can reduce development time and costs, and create more competitive products that can be easily adapted to different use cases and applications.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues for cusp forms and elliptic curves over finite fields, which is a longstanding issue in number theory. The AI approach involves utilizing the theory of Hardy-Krause variation and formulating a technique to approximate relevant functions, allowing for the study of a large class of joint equidistribution problems. The outcome is a framework for resolving these problems with effective error terms, contributing to the understanding of Sato-Tate laws.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the technique of approximating functions of bounded Hardy-Krause variation to study joint equidistribution problems in other fields, such as cryptography or coding theory. By leveraging the theory of H-K variation, researchers can develop more effective methods for analyzing complex distributions and improving error terms.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity lies in developing cryptographic protocols or coding schemes that utilize the insights gained from this research, offering enhanced security or efficiency. Companies specializing in cybersecurity or data compression could adapt these findings to create innovative products or services, capitalizing on the theoretical advances made in this study.

case_studies.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed, yet their outputs can be highly sensitive to routine, non-adversarial variation in how users phrase queries, a gap not well addressed by existing red-teaming efforts. We propose Green Shielding, a user-centric agenda for building evidence-backed deployment guidance by characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior. We operationalize this agenda through the CUE criteria: benchmarks with authentic Context, reference standards and metrics that capture true Utility, and perturbations that reflect realistic variations in the E
case_studies.summary: The problem of large language models being sensitive to minor variations in user input is addressed through the proposal of Green Shielding, a user-centric approach that aims to build evidence-backed deployment guidance. The AI approach involves characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior using the CUE criteria, which includes benchmarks with authentic context, utility, and perturbations that reflect realistic variations. The outcome of this approach is expected to lead to more trustworthy and reliable AI models that can handle routine variations in user input.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can start by identifying and characterizing the types of benign input variations that are likely to occur in their specific use case, and then use the CUE criteria to develop benchmarks and metrics that capture the true utility of their model. By doing so, they can develop more robust and reliable AI models that are less sensitive to minor variations in user input.
case_studies.monetisation: The Green Shielding approach has the potential to be monetized as a consultancy service or a software product that helps organizations develop more reliable and trustworthy AI models, which can lead to cost savings and increased efficiency. Additionally, the approach can be used to develop more robust and reliable chatbots and virtual assistants that can better handle user input variations, leading to improved customer satisfaction and loyalty.
case_studies.relevance_tag: NLP, MLOps, AI Agents, LLMs, Safety

case_studies.title: Can Current Agents Close the Discovery-to-Application Gap? A Case Study in Minecraft
case_studies.abstract: Discovering causal regularities and applying them to build functional systems--the discovery-to-application loop--is a hallmark of general intelligence, yet evaluating this capacity has been hindered by the vast complexity gap between scientific discovery and real-world engineering. We introduce SciCrafter, a Minecraft-based benchmark that operationalizes this loop through parameterized redstone circuit tasks. Agents must ignite lamps in specified patterns (e.g., simultaneously or in timed sequences); scaling target parameters substantially increases construction complexity and required knowle
case_studies.summary: The discovery-to-application gap is a significant challenge in achieving general intelligence, where agents struggle to apply discovered causal regularities to build functional systems. To address this, the authors introduce SciCrafter, a Minecraft-based benchmark that tests an agent's ability to ignite lamps in specified patterns through parameterized redstone circuit tasks. The outcome of this study provides insights into the capabilities and limitations of current agents in closing the discovery-to-application gap.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by using Minecraft-based benchmarks like SciCrafter to evaluate and improve the performance of their agents in complex, real-world-like tasks. By doing so, they can identify areas where their agents need improvement and develop targeted solutions to enhance their agents' capabilities.
case_studies.monetisation: The SciCrafter benchmark has the potential to be developed into a commercial product or service, offering a unique evaluation tool for AI agents and robotics systems. Companies can leverage this technology to test and improve the performance of their AI-powered systems, particularly in applications that require complex problem-solving and sequential decision-making.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
case_studies.abstract: This paper investigates whether source trustworthiness shapes Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models (LLMs) track this sensitivity. We study the past-domain contrast between -DI and -mIs in controlled cloze contexts where the information source is overtly external, while only its perceived reliability is manipulated (High-Trust vs. Low-Trust). In a human production experiment, native speakers of Turkish show a robust trust effect: High-Trust contexts yield relatively more -DI, whereas Low-Trust contexts yield relatively more -mIs, with the pattern remaining stable acro
case_studies.summary: The study investigates how source trustworthiness affects Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models (LLMs) can track this sensitivity. The researchers used a controlled cloze context experiment to manipulate the perceived reliability of the information source and analyzed the responses of native Turkish speakers and LLMs. The results show a robust trust effect, with High-Trust contexts yielding more -DI and Low-Trust contexts yielding more -mIs, but the practical applications of this research are still largely theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by incorporating source trustworthiness into their language models to improve their performance in tasks that require evidential reasoning. However, further research is needed to develop practical methods for manipulating source trustworthiness in real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has limited monetisation potential at this stage, as it is primarily focused on understanding the theoretical aspects of source-sensitive reasoning in Turkish. However, the findings could be used to develop more accurate language models for the Turkish market, which could have potential applications in industries such as language translation and chatbots.

case_studies.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
case_studies.abstract: As human-AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent's perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted
case_studies.summary: The problem of measuring successful cooperation in human-AI teamwork is addressed through the development of two scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale. The AI approach involves grounding these scales in joint activity theory and evolutionary cooperation theory to capture the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction. The outcome is the introduction of two theoretically grounded scales that can be used to assess the quality of human-AI cooperation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale to evaluate the effectiveness of their human-AI teamwork systems and identify areas for improvement. By using these scales, practitioners can develop more effective human-AI collaboration systems that take into account the subjective experience of human team members.
case_studies.monetisation: The Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale can be licensed to companies developing human-AI collaboration systems, providing a potential revenue stream. Additionally, the scales can be used as a basis for developing new products or services that focus on improving human-AI teamwork, such as training programs or collaboration software.

case_studies.title: Multiple positive solutions with prescribed masses for a coupled Schrödinger system: mass mixed and Sobolev critical coupled case
case_studies.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish multiple positive normalized solutions $(u,v,λ_1,λ_2)\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N,\mathbb{R}^2)\times \mathbb{R}^2$ to the following coupled Schrödinger system involving Sobolev critical exponent: $$ \begin{cases} -Δu+λ_1 u=μ_1|u|^{p-2}u+να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^β, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ -Δv+λ_2 v=μ_2|v|^{q-2}v+νβ|v|^{β-2}v|u|^α, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\mathrm{d}x=a, \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v|^2\mathrm{d}x=b, \end{cases} N\geq 3, $$ where $μ_1,μ_2, ν, a, b>0$. We are particularly interested in the mass mixed case that $2<p, q<2+\frac{4}{N}, α>1, β>1$, and $
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed is the existence of multiple positive normalized solutions to a coupled Schrödinger system involving Sobolev critical exponent. The AI approach involves analyzing the system using mathematical techniques such as variational methods and Nash-Moser theory. The outcome is the establishment of multiple positive normalized solutions under certain conditions.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can use variational methods and Nash-Moser theory to analyze complex systems and establish the existence of solutions. Additionally, they can consider the mass mixed and Sobolev critical coupled case to better understand the behavior of such systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has limited monetization potential as it is primarily theoretical and focused on a specific mathematical problem. However, the techniques and methods developed can be applied to other fields such as physics and engineering, which could lead to potential business opportunities in the future.
